## Purpose
The self-registering capability registry: the single authoritative `(kind, name)` membership set the workflow compiler validates every manifest capability reference against, plus the lazy machinery that binds each name to its runtime implementation.

## Shape
- `_KNOWN` — a module-import-time literal set of every valid `(kind, name)` pair (strategy, validator, deliverable, tool, gate, skill, hook, mcp_server, etc.); populated with zero implementations bound, so the compiler can validate manifests without pulling in any impl code.
- `register(kind, name, *, user_allowed=..., description=..., config_schema=...)` — a class decorator that binds `(kind, name) → impl instance` into `_IMPLS`, records the `user_allowed` trust flag into `_TRUST`, and records display metadata into `_META`.
- `discover()` — explicitly imports the known capability subpackages (no auto-discovery/entry-point magic) so their `@register` decorators fire; idempotent, invoked lazily at first `execute()`/`resolve()`, never at compiler import time; a forward-surface package that fails to import degrades to "unavailable" rather than aborting all discovery.
- `CapabilityRegistry` — the query surface: `is_registered` (pure `_KNOWN` membership), `is_user_allowed` (trust check, defaults to `False`), `describe` (display metadata), `resolve` (static dict lookup into `_IMPLS`, raising `KeyError` for an unknown name and `RuntimeError` for a known-but-undiscovered one), and `resolve_alias` (delegates the `od_prototype → prototype` id alias to `agents.registry`).

## Why this shape
`_KNOWN` (membership) and `_IMPLS` (implementation) are deliberately separate registries so the compiler's manifest-validation path stays import-light and side-effect-free, while `resolve()` performs a pure static dict lookup with no dynamic name resolution — explicitly called out in the module docstring as a security property (no attribute fetch, expression evaluation, or dynamic import from untrusted manifest strings).
